requiredFindings.title: The replacement cap and margin rule needs an explicit law gate
requiredFindings.detail: r4's stated return-to-law trigger has fired. r5 now adopts a different population/corpus cap rule, adds power-of-two rounding and exempts over-item-5 entries from the margin obligation. M3-C item 2 asks for a maximum-population recipe derivation and extends the T2 margin test; it does not explicitly select this new empirical formula or qualification exception. M3-B r6 is a precedent for a separately reviewed law amendment selecting caps after measured options, not for silently adopting a replacement rule in an implementation plan.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Gate C1a4's cap selection/profile publication on an accepted M3-C r9 law record (or equivalent explicit law revision). Have it settle the derivation population, empirical T2 role, rounding rule, over-item-5 classification and margin coverage, and the rejected alternatives. C1a1–3 may remain scoped preparatory library/model work without a production snapshot-profile claim.

requiredFindings.title: The item-5 reference population and its full charge are not defined
requiredFindings.detail: Term (a) is described as 100,000 rows whose canonical inventory is at most 4 MiB. No such inventory exists: the 64-character digest values alone take 6,400,000 bytes before paths, keys and framing. It could instead be a conservative componentwise envelope, but the plan must say so and define its formula. Row count and total payload also do not determine directory/listing, excluded-name, ACL, repeated-copy, read-attempt and custody work. The current C1a1 model predicts the walk only; read, retention and custody terms are explicitly still to be added.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Define (a) as either a feasible admissible-population optimization or an explicitly conservative componentwise bound, with the full descriptor envelope distinguished from inventory bytes. Specify all operation counts and worst-branch charges, including directory/non-inventory work, bounded short-read/Interrupted/EOF attempts and C1a2's custody/capture/row costs. Do not substitute a typical or impossible tree for the normative population. Make completion and review of this formula a prerequisite to the cap calculation.

requiredFindings.title: One blind run cannot both choose an unknown cap and bind its later closure change as ordered
requiredFindings.detail: C1a4 evaluates held-out maximum (c), uses it to choose the cap, then changes snapshot_profile/work_ledger.rs and re-pins the census. It nevertheless promises one gated blind run that both supplies (c) and refreshes the discovery receipt against those final bytes. Under B2-b4 plan r6 section 2.5 the receipt binds current caps, tool bytes and every closure pin, including work_ledger.rs. A measurement before the final cap is written is stale after that change; a final receipt run after the change cannot be the earlier run that first supplied the unknown maximum.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Specify a non-circular, pre-reviewed protocol. For example, use a separately reviewed blind derivation phase with an explicitly allowed closed output, then freeze the law-approved caps and closure pins, followed by the reviewed final receipt run; or choose caps entirely before a single final validation run and return failures to the law. Name all reviews, outputs, staleness transitions and run counts. Do not expose raw held-out counts or imply a changed-pin receipt remains current.
